Log to a rotating file

Source: R/Appender.R
AppenderFileRotating.Rd

An extension of AppenderFile that rotates logfiles based on certain conditions. Please refer to the documentation of rotor::rotate() for the meanings of the extra arguments

See also

AppenderFileRotatingDate, AppenderFileRotatingTime, rotor::rotate()

Other Appenders: Appender, AppenderBuffer, AppenderConsole, AppenderFile, AppenderFileRotatingDate, AppenderFileRotatingTime, AppenderTable

Super classes

Filterable -> Appender -> AppenderFile -> AppenderFileRotating

Active bindings

size

The maximum size of the log file that triggers rotation. See $set_size().

create_file

Defunct, do not use.

compression

Whether backups are compressed. See $set_compression().

max_backups

The maximum number of backups to keep. See $set_max_backups().

backups

A data.frame containing information on path, file size, etc... on the available backups of file.

backup_dir

The directory that backups are stored in. See $set_backup_dir().

AppenderFileRotating$new()

Create a new AppenderFileRotating.

Usage

AppenderFileRotating$new(
  file,
  threshold = NA_integer_,
  layout = LayoutFormat$new(),
  filters = NULL,
  size = Inf,
  max_backups = Inf,
  compression = FALSE,
  backup_dir = dirname(file),
  create_file = NULL
)

Arguments

file

character scalar. Path to the log file. If file does not exist it will be created.

threshold

character or integer scalar. The minimum log level that triggers this Appender. See log_levels.

layout

A Layout that determines how LogEvents are formatted before being output by this Appender.

filters

A list of EventFilters or predicate functions used to filter events for this Appender. See Filterable.

size, max_backups, compression, backup_dir

see rotor::rotate() for the meaning of these arguments. Note that backup_dir corresponds to dir.

create_file

Defunct, do not use.

AppenderFileRotating$append()

Process a LogEvent event by appending it to $file, then rotate the file if necessary (see $rotate()). This method is usually not called by the user, but invoked by a Logger.

Usage

AppenderFileRotating$append(event)

Arguments

event

a LogEvent

AppenderFileRotating$rotate()

Rotate the log file if it meets the rotation conditions (see $size), or unconditionally if force = TRUE. See rotor::rotate() for details.

Usage

AppenderFileRotating$rotate(force = FALSE)

Arguments

force

TRUE or FALSE. Force rotation regardless of whether the rotation conditions are met.

AppenderFileRotating$prune()

Remove old backups so that at most max_backups remain. See rotor::rotate().

Usage

AppenderFileRotating$prune(max_backups = self$max_backups)

Arguments

max_backups

integer scalar. Defaults to $max_backups.

AppenderFileRotating$set_size()

Set the maximum size of the log file that triggers rotation. See rotor::rotate().

Usage

AppenderFileRotating$set_size(x)

Arguments

x

A numeric file size in bytes, a character scalar such as "5mb" (see rotor::rotate()), or Inf to disable size-based rotation.

Arguments

x

integer scalar >= 0, or Inf to keep all backups.
